subject: Post-call: HorizonMed eval checklist + dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@horizonmed.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + scope (HorizonMed)

Thanks for the call today, Rachel — useful discussion. A quick recap from our side:

- Primary goal: reduce inference cost for real-time clinical suggestions while keeping p95 latency under 200ms.
- Current vendors: testing CloudScale endpoints (reserved GPUs) and Inferly API for embeddings.
- Procurement preference: if we go reserved, legal needs a clear commitment model and SLAs. If cloud burst is cheaper, we need cost math and failure modes.

Can you send the post-call checklist and a proposed test plan that demonstrates: baseline latency, 99th/95th latency under load, cold-start behavior, and a failover run to your hosted fallback? Also curious how Redwood’s dedicated pools handle preemption vs CloudScale reserved slots.

Avery
Director of ML Infrastructure
HorizonMed
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@horizonmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-call: HorizonMed eval checklist + dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Great to connect, Avery — appreciate the clear priorities. Attaching a lightweight metrics template and our eval checklist to frame the tests. High-level proposal below, happy to adjust: 

1) Baseline run (hosted API): 2 hours steady traffic mimicking 30 RPS, capture p50/p95/p99 token latencies, token cost breakdown.
2) Dedicated smoke (reserved capacity): 1-hour warm steady run on a dedicated pool sized to match 30 RPS; record latency and utilization.
3) Stress and tail behavior: incremental increase to 120 RPS to observe queuing, throttles, and autoscaling time (if applicable).
4) Cold-start and KV-cache test: restart model instances and run synthetic traffic to measure cold-start tail; test prefix/KV cache hit/miss scenarios.
5) Failover run: route 20% of traffic to hosted fallback and compare error/latency profiles.

Key differentiation we'll demonstrate vs CloudScale: predictable reuse of warmed KV cache on dedicated pools, model-variant fallback policies, and transparent token-level cost breakdowns. For procurement, we’ll outline reserved vs burst pricing options and a sample SLA.

Next steps: can you confirm which business unit will run the tests (ML infra vs app teams) and provide a small test dataset or sample queries? Also confirm a 2-hour block next week for the baseline run.

Attachments: postcall-metrics-template.csv, redwood-dedicated-eval-checklist.md

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Collins <avery.collins@horizonmed.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: HorizonMed eval checklist + dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Looping in Logan to scope the runbook; initial notes from SRE/bench team below. Rachel — feel free to forward this to Avery as a working plan.

Runbook (concise):
- Pre-test: ingest sample prompts (anonymized), confirm model version and sequence length distribution.
- Baseline (hosted): 2h steady at target QPS (we'll supply a trace-replay tool). Collect token-level billing, per-request traces, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): provision a 2-GPU low-latency pool (A100/80GB quantized profile) for warm-run; measure p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rates.
- Stress: linear ramp to 4x target over 30 min; observe scheduler queuing behavior and circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Cold-start: rotate 20% of nodes and run a short spike to profile cold tails.
- Failover test: simulate a control-plane throttle and shift 20% to hosted fallback. Verify rollout policies and error budgets.

Success criteria we recommend: p95 <= 200ms (target), sustained <= 1.2x token cost vs hosted for dedicated, and no more than 2% error increase during failover.

Data/permits: we need a signed test access form from HorizonMed to provision private test pools and ingest sample traces. Rachel — can you confirm who in procurement will sign?

Attachments we'll provide: dedicated-test-runbook.pdf, pricing-diff-summary.xlsx

—Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@horizonmed.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: HorizonMed eval checklist + dedicated vs hyperscaler next steps

Thanks all — quick scheduling and tech notes: 

- Availability: Wed 2026-11-25 10:00–14:00 PT is open for baseline + dedicated smoke (we can split into two 90-min blocks).
- Test harness: we'll share a recorder and a small load generator that reproduces your p95 requests.
- Differences vs CloudScale to validate during runs: 
  * Preemption: CloudScale reserved slots may show lower latency variance while preemptible; Redwood dedicated pools are tenant-isolated with no GPU preemption for reserved customers.
  * Burst strategy: With Redwood you can reserve base capacity + configured burst rails to hyperscalers; we'll include a simulated cross-region burst to show routing/fallback latency.
  * Observability: Token-level cost attribution and per-request traces (we'll push a trace export to your S3).

Logistics ask: please provide an S3 path with sample queries (anonymized) and a contact for procurement. If HorizonMed prefers an NDA/test access form first, we'll work through it — otherwise we can proceed with a sanitized public dataset.

Next immediate action items:
- Rachel: confirm the time slot (Wed 11/25 10:00 PT) with Avery.
- Avery: share S3 sample or confirm NDA.
- Marissa: finalize runbook and provide short pricing sheet for reserved vs burst (I'll validate GPU SKU selection).

Looking forward — we’ll make sure the plan highlights the exact head-to-head points you care about vs CloudScale.

—Logan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
